newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe to get sixth commercial bank next year.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe to get sixth commercial bank next year.

text.p: A consortium of Zimbabwean professional bankers and some leading local corporate investors plan to open the country's sixth commercial bank next February, one of the bank's principal promoters said on Wednesday.
Francis Nhema told reporters the state registrar of banks had approved the establishment of Time Bank of Zimbabwe in which professional bankers Time Investment Company would be the major shareholder.
Other shareholders include two local insurance companies, four pension funds and a foreign bank, which Nhema declined to name.
The bank would have an initial capital of Z$55 million and its authorised share capital would be Z$100 million.

Nhema, who is managing dircetor of the Zimbabwe Building Society, said the new bank was set up in response to a growing need for financial services for the country's small to medium-scale enterprise sector.

"We intend to negotiate with some of our shareholders to utilise their funds and I think the government will be willing to negotiate on that issue so that funds held by pension funds can be channeled for small enterprise development," he said.
"We hope the bank will be used as a facility for channeling donor funds to indigenous (black) businesses," he said.

Zimbabwe's banking sector is flourishing with new arrivals. One commercial bank, six merchant banks, four discount houses, two building societies and one finance house have been established since 1980.
Two more commercial banks, OMA Bank, and Progressive Commercial Bank -- both organised by women fighting for black economic empowerment -- are also expected to be established next year.
